Extract values from a SpatRaster

Source: R/extract_by_coord.R
extract_by_coord.Rd

Extract values from a SpatRaster for a set of locations. The locations must be a point SpatVector.

Usage

extract_by_coord(
  raster,
  coord,
  iteration = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  buffer = NULL,
  fn = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  chunk = "auto",
  ...
)

Arguments

raster

A SpatRaster. Each layer becomes one column of the result.

coord

A point SpatVector carrying the unit identifier, typically created with georef_coord().

iteration

Deprecated; use label.

id

Optional character string naming the column that identifies the units. When NULL, ID is used, or ID_adm_div when that is the only one present.

buffer

Optional distance in metres around each location to summarise.

fn

Summary over a buffer: "mean", "sum", "mode", "min", "max" or a function. Defaults from the kind of variable.

label

Optional name shown in progress messages.

chunk

"auto" extracts in blocks of layers only when needed; a whole number forces that many layers per block; FALSE never splits.

...

additional arguments to pass to terra::extract.

Value

A c4e_tbl with the extracted values for each location and the coordinates of its cell (x_cell, y_cell). If the raster has multiple layers, the values of the layer will be split by columns.

Details

The result is a c4e_tbl that carries the raster's context: variable, unit, time step, dates, CRS and data source, as recorded by read_climate(). Later steps read their defaults from it.

The raster and the locations must share a CRS. Locations outside the raster, or on cells that are missing in every layer, are reported with their identifiers.

With buffer, each location gets a summary of the cells within that distance instead of the value of its own cell: the mean for continuous variables, the sum for counts (population) and the most frequent value for categories, unless fn says otherwise.

When the result would exceed the memory budget (see ?c4e), the layers are extracted in blocks and bound together, with a progress bar.

See also

extract, extract_by_poly(), extract_cell_by_poly()

Examples

tmax <- read_climate(
  system.file("extdata", "tmax_daily.tif", package = "c4e"))
#> Read tmax_daily: tmax [K], daily, 2021-01-01 to 2023-12-31, 1095 layers
#> (synthetic).
survey <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
coord <- prepare_coord(survey, lat_var = lat, lon_var = lon)
points <- georef_coord(coord, geom = c("lon", "lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")

extract_by_coord(tmax[[1:5]], points)
#> # A tibble: 12 × 8
#> # Context:  tmax [K], day, wide; key ID
#>    ID          x_cell y_cell `2021-01-01` `2021-01-02` `2021-01-03` `2021-01-04`

#>  1 30.87620_-…   30.9   -0.9         296.         298.         296.         299.
#>  2 30.45000_-…   30.5   -0.7         295.         292.         292.         293.
#>  3 30.85840_-…   30.9   -0.3         295.         296.         298.         295.
#>  4 30.77090_-…   30.7   -0.3         294.         295.         299.         297.
#>  5 30.43250_-…   30.5   -0.3         292.         294.         294.         293.
#>  6 30.41290_-…   30.5   -0.3         292.         294.         294.         293.
#>  7 30.38170_-…   30.3   -0.3         293.         293.         296.         294.
#>  8 30.68870_-…   30.7   -0.1         293.         294.         295.         295.
#>  9 30.27330_-…   30.3   -0.1         293.         295.         294.         292.
#> 10 30.51990_0…   30.5    0.1         290.         296.         293.         290.
#> 11 30.89740_0…   30.9    0.1         295.         294.         293.         293.
#> 12 30.41520_0…   30.5    0.1         290.         296.         293.         290.
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: `2021-01-05` <dbl>

# the mean of the cells within 20 km of each location
extract_by_coord(tmax[[1:5]], points, buffer = 20000)
